items.title: Conseil des ministres du 02/09/2026 : FMI, JOJ…le Président Bassirou Diomaye Faye trace la feuille de route de la rentrée
items.description: Réuni ce mercredi 2 septembre 2026 au Palais de la République, le Conseil des ministres a été marqué par une communication fournie du Chef de l'État, Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye, qui a passé en revue les principaux dossiers économiques, sociaux et sportifs du moment. Entre l’accord avec le FMI, les Jeux olympiques de la Jeunesse (JOJ) à venir, le pouvoir d'achat des Sénégalais et autres dossiers prioritaires, voici ce qu’il faut retenir de la communication du Président. Un satisfecit pour l'accord avec le FMI Le Président a salué l'accord technique de principe conclu entre Dakar et le Fonds monétaire international, appelé à soutenir les réformes économiques et financières engagées. D’ailleurs, cette mobilisation, projetée au titre de la « Facilité élargie de crédit (FEC) d'un montant de 1243 milliards de FCFA (soit 2,2 milliards USD) sur une période de trois (03) ans », a valu au Premier ministre et à son équipe économique les félicitations du Chef de l'État « pour le travail accompli et les résultats obtenus ». Pouvoir d'achat et cherté de la vie au cœur des priorités Dans sa communication, Bassirou Diomaye Faye insiste sur l'importance qu’il accorde à « la préservation du pouvoir d'achat des ménages » et à « la mise en œuvre de mesures de lutte contre la cherté de la vie ». Il a par ailleurs demandé une application rigoureuse des « instruments adaptés de la loi sur les prix et la protection du Consommateur », et souligné l'impératif de « réguler les coûts des loyers » grâce à des dispositifs réglementaires renforcés. En outre, le Président Faye souligne « l’impératif de mener une réflexion stratégique sur le financement durable de la Couverture sanitaire universelle (CSU), la revalorisation des pensions de retraite et la préservation des acquis liés à la gouvernance des institutions de protection sociale». Pour ce faire, il « «demande de renforcer le Fonds de Solidarité nationale et le Commissariat à la Sécurité Alimentaire et à la Résilience et d’actualiser le cadre de pilotage et de suivi des impacts sociaux des entités, programmes et projets de promotion de l’équité». Investissement et hydrocarbures sous surveillance Pour améliorer le climat des affaires, le Chef de l'État a demandé au Premier ministre de préparer « la tenue prochaine du Conseil Présidentiel de l'Investissement (CPI) ». Sur le volet énergétique, il a annoncé « la tenue prochaine d'une session spéciale du COS-PETROGAZ » et réclamé l'activation des instances de pilotage du Fonds Intergénérationnel. Jeunesse, emploi et rentrée scolaire Rappelant ses priorités « Jeunesse, Employabilité et Emploi », le Président a exhorté le gouvernement à accélérer l'ancrage de la formation duale et la réalisation des centres de formation professionnelle. Il a également demandé de veiller à « la bonne préparation des prochaines rentrées scolaire et universitaire » et de finaliser le projet de loi de finances 2027. JOJ Dakar 2026 : cap sur la mobilisation générale Après l'inauguration, le 29 août, du Village olympique et du Centre équestre de Diamniadio, le Chef de l'État a félicité le Premier ministre et plusieurs membres du gouvernement « pour les efforts consentis afin de livrer les travaux dans les délais ». Il a conclu sa communication par « un appel à la mobilisation nationale autour de l'appropriation et du succès des JOJ Dakar 2026 ». O.B.N

items.title: Travelers with multiple new devices returning to Ghana to pay additional charges – Customs Commissioner
items.description: Travelers returning to Ghana with multiple new devices including mobile phones and other electronic gadgets may be compelled to pay commercial duties on such products at the airport during arrival processes. Briefing journalists after a tour of the Airport, Commissioner of Customs at the Ghana Revenue Authority, Aaron Kanor, said more than two mobile devices could amount to commercial use. The Commissioner also disclosed plans to fully automate passenger profiling at the country’s airports during arrivals. He noted that this is part of international customs as such items are required to be declared by the owners. “In Ghana, because of our culture, when one is traveling, Amma gives you one phone, Kofi gives you another and all the days born phones, they all give you phones. When you carry all those seven phones and you arrive, it will amount to what? Commercial. “This is because as an individual, you are entitled to one or maybe two, considering that the other is for your wife”. “So, we implore that when you are coming home, you do not collect people’s things. If you collect them and they are beyond two, one is allowed to carry two”, he added. “One for yourself and maybe one for your wife. Beyond that, it amounts to commercial because all these phones are expensive”, he mentioned. Furthermore, he said, “If you look at iPhone, Samsung, they are very expensive. That is where we can get our revenue”. Meanwhile, the Customs Division of the GRA is in the process to fully automate passenger profiling at the country’s airports during arrivals. This is part of the transformation of the GRA and to help curb delays at the ports as a result of customs physical checks.

items.title: John Boadu: A lifetime of party service, experience and grassroots leadership
items.description: For decades, John Boadu has occupied some of the most important organisational positions within Ghana’s New Patriotic Party (NPP), building a political career that has taken him from the grassroots to the highest levels of the party’s national structure. His journey is one marked not only by positions held, but also by the experiences gathered along the way experiences that have exposed him to electoral victories, political setbacks, internal party challenges and the continuous task of keeping a large political organisation together. As the NPP considers its future leadership, Boadu’s record places him among the experienced figures whose understanding of the party’s organisational structure is difficult to overlook. His political experience stretches across several layers of the party. He has served as Youth Organiser, National Organiser, Acting General Secretary and General Secretary, among other responsibilities. These positions have given him exposure to the practical workings of the party, from grassroots mobilisation and polling-station structures to constituency, regional and national administration. For a political organisation whose electoral fortunes depend heavily on the effectiveness of its grassroots structures, such experience can be significant. Boadu’s years in party organisation have also brought him into contact with polling-station executives, constituency leaders, regional executives, national officers, party activists and government officials during periods when the NPP has been in power. That broad network of relationships is an important part of his political profile. Politics, however, is not simply about occupying an office. It is also about relationships, communication and the ability to work with people who may not always share the same opinions. Throughout his political career, Boadu has operated within an environment where disagreements, competing ambitions and differing interpretations of the party’s direction are inevitable. His experience therefore includes navigating the human side of political organisation, engaging individuals and groups across different levels of the party. That experience has been particularly relevant to his interactions with the grassroots. The polling station executive remains one of the most important actors in Ghanaian electoral politics. It is at the polling-station level that national political strategies are ultimately translated into votes. Candidates may make speeches at national rallies, but the actual work of mobilising voters, monitoring polling stations and maintaining contact with communities is largely carried out by people at the grassroots. Boadu’s long association with party organisation has therefore provided him with considerable familiarity with this structure. His relationship with the youth is another feature of his political profile. Having served as a Youth Organiser, Boadu has had direct experience working with younger party members and understanding their role in political mobilisation. The youth constitute a significant component of every political organisation, but they also represent one of the groups most interested in questions of employment, economic opportunity, political participation and leadership succession. His experience has consequently placed him in a position to understand the importance of bringing young people into the party’s organisational and decision-making processes rather than treating them merely as campaign foot soldiers. Perhaps one of the most significant aspects of Boadu’s political journey is that it has not been confined to one particular phase of the NPP’s history. He has experienced the party in opposition and has also participated in periods when the NPP controlled government. He has therefore witnessed the contrasting demands that come with political power and opposition. When a party is in government, expectations from its supporters and grassroots members can be enormous. Constituency and polling-station activists expect communication, recognition and responsiveness, while government officials must simultaneously deal with the responsibilities of governance. In opposition, the priorities change. Organisation, unity, mobilisation and rebuilding become particularly important. Boadu’s experience across these different political environments has contributed to his understanding of the relationship between the party organisation and government. Yet his record should also be viewed within the broader history of the NPP. Like every senior political figure, his career has been associated with both achievements and difficult moments. The party has enjoyed major electoral victories during periods in which he held senior organisational responsibilities, but it has also suffered electoral defeats. Those contrasting experiences can provide valuable lessons. Victory can create confidence, while defeat can expose organisational weaknesses that may otherwise remain hidden. A leader who has experienced both is inevitably confronted with questions about what worked, what failed and what must change. As the NPP looks toward the future, these questions are particularly important. The challenge before the party is not simply to select individuals for positions. It is to determine what kind of organisational leadership is required to strengthen its structures, rebuild confidence, improve communication and reconnect effectively with members at every level. That conversation inevitably brings attention to individuals with long institutional experience. John Boadu’s political profile is therefore rooted in several decades of party service, organisational responsibility and relationships across the NPP’s structures. His experience from the youth wing to national administration, from grassroots mobilisation to senior party leadership, gives him an understanding of the organisation that has been developed over many years. Ultimately, the assessment of any candidate for national party leadership must go beyond slogans and promises. It requires consideration of experience, organisational competence, temperament, relationships, understanding of the grassroots and the ability to work with different constituencies within the party. For John Boadu, the record provides a substantial basis for that assessment. His political journey represents a long chapter in the organisational history of the NPP, a journey shaped by service, responsibility, electoral campaigns, leadership challenges, relationships and lessons from both success and defeat. As the party debates its next chapter, that experience will remain an important part of the conversation about the leadership and direction of the NPP.

items.title: Ceuta se echa a la calle para exigir soluciones a la crisis migratoria
items.description: Ceuta ha salido a la calle este miércoles en una gran manifestación para exigir soluciones que devuelvan la normalidad a una ciudad que lleva más de un mes sometida a una fuerte presión migratoria. Los ceutíes han estado calentando motores durante una semana, con una batería de protestas y actos de reivindicación. Pero la convocatoria del 2 de septiembre, día de la ciudad autónoma, era la gran apuesta para visibilizar el descontento de una ciudad de 83.000 habitantes que sigue sufriendo los efectos de la entrada multitudinaria del 30 y 31 de julio de más de 70.000 personas y la permanencia en sus calles de miles de migrantes que hacen vida en sus playas, parques o calles, hasta saber qué será de ellos. La cita ha congregado a unas 20.000 personas, según datos de la Delegación del Gobierno, que han reivindicado durante al menos tres horas su identidad propia y pertenencia a España. Entre fuertes críticas a la gestión del Ejecutivo, los manifestantes han reclamado la expulsión de los migrantes y que se les defienda frente a Marruecos. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Diplomatie | Mohamed Ali Nafti reçoit la nouvelle ambassadrice des Pays-Bas à Tunis
items.description: Mohamed Ali Nafti, Ministre des Affaires Étrangères, de la Migration et des Tunisiens à l’Étranger, a reçu, le 2 septembre 2026, au siège du Ministère, Dewi van de Weerd, qui lui a remis une copie figurée de ses Lettres de Créance en sa qualité d'Ambassadrice du Royaume des Pays-Bas en Tunisie. Au cours de cet entretien, le Ministre a salué les relations d'amitié et de coopération de longue date et distinguées existant entre les deux Pays, dont les racines remontent à la fin du 17ème siècle, se félicitant de l'évolution remarquable qu'elles ont connue au cours des dernières années dans plusieurs secteurs vitaux, tels que l'agriculture, l'eau, l'environnement, le développement durable, l’emploi et les programmes d'insertion des jeunes et des femmes. Il a réitéré, à cette occasion, le souci de la Tunisie de renforcer la coopération avec ce Pays ami dans les différents domaines d'intérêt commun, y compris scientifiques et académiques. Le Ministre s'est également félicité du niveau du partenariat et des investissements existants avec les Pays-Bas, signalant que 101 entreprises économiques opèrent dans notre Pays sous forme d'investissements directs ou conjoints, générant environ 20 mille postes d’emploi. Il a exprimé l'aspiration à un flux accru d'investissements néerlandais dans des secteurs porteurs et prioritaires pour notre Pays, notamment les énergies renouvelables et l'environnement, à la lumière des incitations et des avantages comparatifs qu'offre notre Pays à cet égard. Pour sa part, l'Ambassadrice des Pays-Bas a confirmé sa détermination à développer davantage la coopération entre les deux Pays, à en élargir la base et à en diversifier les domaines, mettant en relief l’engagement de son Pays de continuer à renforcer les relations de partenariat avec la Tunisie dans les divers domaines économiques, culturels, scientifiques et académiques, au service des intérêts communs des deux Peuples amis. Communiqué L’article Diplomatie | Mohamed Ali Nafti reçoit la nouvelle ambassadrice des Pays-Bas à Tunis est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Russie-Iran: le Président Poutine salue le courage du peuple iranien et réaffirme le soutien de Moscou à Téhéran
items.description: RUSSIE-IRAN-POUTINE-SALUE-COURAGE-PEUPLE-IRANIEN Russie-Iran: le Président Poutine salue le courage du peuple iranien et réaffirme le soutien de Moscou à Téhéran Ouagadougou, 2 sept. 2026 (AIB) – Le Président russe Vladimir Poutine a exprimé, mardi 1er septembre 2026 à Bichkek, capitale du Kirghizstan, la solidarité de Moscou avec le peuple iranien, saluant son courage et sa résilience dans la défense de ses intérêts nationaux. Il a également réaffirmé le soutien de la Russie à Téhéran dans cette période difficile. Vladimir Poutine s’exprimait lors d’un entretien avec son homologue iranien, Massoud Pezechkian, en marge du sommet de l’Organisation de coopération de Shanghai (OCS), tenu les 31 août et 1er septembre 2026 à Bichkek. « En Russie, nous sommes solidaires du peuple iranien. Nous admirons votre courage et votre résilience dans la lutte pour vos intérêts nationaux », a déclaré le président russe. Il a assuré que Moscou continuerait d’apporter son soutien à Téhéran, à travers la fourniture des biens nécessaires dont l’Iran a besoin. Le Président russe a également transmis au président iranien ses salutations ainsi que ses « paroles de soutien sincère » au Guide suprême de la République islamique d’Iran, Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei. Vladimir Poutine a par ailleurs évoqué le cessez-le-feu conclu en juin entre l’Iran et les États-Unis, estimant que cette avancée, saluée par Moscou, demeurait fragile et instable. De son côté, Massoud Pezechkian a remercié la Russie pour son soutien à l’Iran dans les instances internationales, pendant le conflit avec les États-Unis et face aux sanctions américaines. Le Président iranien a réaffirmé que son pays n’était pas à l’origine de la guerre avec Washington et que Téhéran privilégiait la diplomatie et les négociations pour régler les différends. Il a toutefois insisté sur la nécessité d’obtenir des garanties permettant d’assurer le respect de tout éventuel accord. Les deux dirigeants ont souligné le caractère stratégique de leurs relations et la nécessité de renforcer leur coopération bilatérale et multilatérale au sein de l’OCS. Vladimir Poutine a relevé la poursuite du développement des relations russo-iraniennes dans plusieurs domaines, notamment les échanges commerciaux. Il a aussi évoqué l’accord de libre-échange entre l’Iran et l’Union économique eurasiatique (UEEA). Agence d'Information du Burkina Source: RT

items.title: Ghana to host 16th African Economic Summit as Friends of Africa brings Global Investment Dialogue to Accra
items.description: From boardrooms to start-up pitches, Ghana is preparing to become the meeting point for investors, governments, entrepreneurs and businesses from Africa and North America as the Friends of Africa Economic Summit makes its Ghanaian debut with an ambitious mission: “Turning partnerships and ideas into sustainable investment opportunities.” Ghana is set to host the 16th African Economic Summit, marking a major milestone in the Friends of Africa (FOA) initiative as the organisation brings 15 years of experience hosting economic summits in North America to the African continent. The two-day Friends of Africa Economic Summit 2026 is scheduled for September 17–18, 2026, at the Kempinski Hotel Gold Coast City in Accra, under the theme, “Building Sustainable Futures: Scaling Investment Partnerships in Ghana.” The summit is expected to bring together business leaders, government representatives, investors, entrepreneurs, founders and professionals for discussions and networking focused on strengthening investment partnerships and creating practical opportunities for economic growth. According to the organisers, the Ghana edition represents an effort to share the experience gained from 15 years of hosting the African Economic Summit in North America with African counterparts, beginning with Ghana. The programme will begin with informal Friends of Africa sessions from September 16–17, including one-on-one meetings with founders. A private reception for speakers and sponsors is also scheduled for September 17. The main programme on September 18 will feature a full-day combination of business, government and investment discussions, including plenary sessions, expert panels, fireside conversations, government-to-government and business-to-business meetings, exhibitions and networking opportunities. One of the major attractions will be a start-up pitch competition featuring 40 start-ups presenting their value propositions before investors and funding groups in the hope of competing for seed capital. The organisers say the summit will also provide a marketplace where selected Canadian companies seeking partnerships in Ghana can connect with professionals and businesses. The discussions are expected to focus on critical areas including funding, partnerships and infrastructure development opportunities, while also providing opportunities for knowledge sharing and business-to-business engagement. Beyond the formal business sessions, the summit will showcase Ghanaian food, music and entrepreneurial talent, adding a cultural dimension to the economic and investment discussions. Friends of Africa is also inviting organisations to participate as sponsors, offering several sponsorship categories ranging from US$3,000 for FOA Supporters to US$20,000 for Platinum Sponsors. The Platinum package includes prominent branding, speaking opportunities, VIP access, marketplace tables, advertising in the FOA Magazine, social media promotion and recognition in the summit’s impact report. Gold Sponsors, at US$10,000, will receive branding opportunities around the pitch competition and opportunities to engage with seed-capital winners, while Silver and Bronze sponsors will receive varying levels of visibility, speaking, networking and marketplace opportunities. The organisation said sponsorship support would help strengthen the FOA platform and facilitate the summit’s broader objectives of connecting businesses, investors and governments. The summit is being led in Ghana by Prof. Odoi Yemoh, Chair of the African Economic Summit Committee, Ghana 2026, alongside Nardos Sebro, Executive Lead for Partnerships and Sponsors at Friends of Africa-Global. With Ghana increasingly seeking to position itself as a destination for investment, entrepreneurship and international business partnerships, the summit could provide an important platform for turning conversations into concrete commercial relationships. At its core, however, the Friends of Africa Economic Summit is presenting a broader proposition: Africa’s economic future will require partnerships that move beyond dialogue and translate ideas, capital and innovation into sustainable opportunities. Organizations interested in participating or sponsoring the summit are encouraged to register early and join this important global conversation on building stronger investment partnerships and expanding opportunities for African businesses to contact Friends of Africa-Global through foaglobal@friendsofafrica.ca or visit the Ghanaian-Canadian Chamber of Commerce for registration and further information.

items.title: “We have stabilised the present; now we must secure the future” — Deputy Finance Minister
items.description: The Deputy Minister for Finance, Thomas Nyarko Ampem, says Ghana must now build on its restored macroeconomic stability and secure a productive, competitive and resilient economy for the next decade. “We have stabilised the present. Now we must secure the future,” he declared. Speaking on behalf of the Minister for Finance, Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, at the Business Roundtable Extended 2026 Executive Dialogue in Accra, Mr Ampem said the country must shift its attention from correcting past economic challenges to expanding production, attracting investment and creating jobs. The dialogue, organised by Ishmael Yamson & Associates, was held under the theme, “After the Corrections: Building Resilient Economic Pillars for the Next Decade.” Mr Ampem identified stronger economic buffers, increased productivity, effective institutions, inclusive growth and a vibrant private sector as essential to protecting the economy against future shocks. He also called for greater value addition, stronger local production and closer links among agriculture, industry, technology and skills. According to him, securing Ghana’s future will require a new partnership between Government and businesses. Government, he said, would provide stability, infrastructure, efficient regulation and fiscal discipline, while the private sector must respond with investment, innovation, productivity, exports and job creation. “That is the partnership we need—a partnership built around a common objective: a productive, competitive and resilient Ghanaian economy,” he stated.

Broadcast journalist and laboratory scientist Emmanuel Samani declares GAMLS General Secretary bid
items.description: Medical laboratory scientist and broadcast journalist Dr Emmanuel Raphael Samani has declared his intention to contest the position of General Secretary of the Ghana Association of Medical Laboratory Scientists (GAMLS) for the 2026–2028 term. Dr Samani says his campaign will focus on making the association more visible, responsive and influential in decisions affecting the medical laboratory profession. Declaring his intention to contest, he said medical laboratory scientists must translate their critical role in patient care into greater influence in policy and institutional decision-making. “We cannot be indispensable in the clinical setting and invisible at the table,” he said. Dr Samani, who has almost a decade of experience in laboratory practice in haematology and clinical chemistry, currently works at the Ghana Armed Forces Critical Care and Emergency Hospital. He believes the General Secretary’s role should extend beyond keeping records and coordinating correspondence to becoming the operational centre of a more responsive professional association. “The General Secretary runs the machinery: the communication, the records, the coordination, the follow-through,” he said. “Run it well and the profession is heard. Run it slowly and it is not.” His proposed reforms include a 72-hour rapid-response rule for matters affecting members, a digitised membership register, transparent reporting of membership dues and a standing engagement calendar with key institutions including the Ministry of Health, Ghana Health Service, Parliament’s Health Committee and the profession’s regulator. He has also outlined a first-100-days plan that includes an audit of the secretariat’s records, a tracker on the implementation of congress resolutions and a written report to members at the end of the first 100 days. Dr Samani says the measures are intended to ensure that campaign promises translate into measurable actions and accountability. Beyond his laboratory practice, Dr Samani has built a public profile through broadcasting and advocacy on issues affecting the medical laboratory profession. His experience in journalism has provided him with a platform to bring professional concerns to a wider audience and engage policymakers and the public on issues surrounding laboratory medicine. During the recent impasse between laboratory physicians and medical laboratory scientists, he convened and hosted a discussion on laboratory leadership which attracted about 1,700 live listeners and more than 2,000 replays. He has subsequently continued to use his media platforms to highlight issues affecting medical laboratory scientists. Dr Samani believes his combined experience in laboratory science and communication could help GAMLS strengthen its public engagement and institutional advocacy. He holds a Doctor of Medical Laboratory Science from the University for Development Studies, an MSc in Communication and International Marketing from KNUST and a BSc in Medical Laboratory Science from the University of Cape Coast. He is also an anchor on JoyNews and has previously been a finalist for the BBC World News Komla Dumor Award. Dr Samani says his ambition is to strengthen GAMLS as an institution rather than make its effectiveness dependent on an individual leader. “No association should depend on the courage of one man with one job,” he said. “That is the fragility I am running to fix. When GAMLS speaks under me, it will speak institutionally, with evidence attached.” He argues that the association needs systems that ensure consistent communication, follow-through on decisions, and sustained engagement with institutions responsible for policies affecting the profession. The GAMLS national elections are scheduled for November 6, 2026, during the association’s National Congress.

items.title: Oppong Nkrumah questions Chief Justice’s ‘unprecedented’ tour of state-owned institutions
items.description: The Member of Parliament for Ofoase-Ayirebi, Kojo Oppong Nkrumah, has questioned Chief Justice Paul Baffoe-Bonnie’s visits to state-owned institutions, describing the development as unprecedented and bewildering. According to the former Information Minister, he was surprised by the Chief Justice’s decision to tour institutions such as the Minerals Income Investment Fund (MIIF) and the Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT), arguing that such engagements were unusual for the Judiciary. Mr Nkrumah made the comments on Asempa FM’s Ekosiisen on Wednesday, September 2, following remarks by the Chief Justice praising the performance of MIIF and other public institutions under the current administration. During a visit to MIIF earlier in the day, Justice Baffoe-Bonnie said some of the developments he had witnessed at state institutions had left him wondering what Ghana had been doing over the past eight years. The Chief Justice said his earlier visit to SSNIT had also reinforced his impression that some public institutions were performing significantly better. However, reacting to the development, Mr Oppong Nkrumah said he could not recall any instance in recent political history where a Chief Justice had embarked on official tours of state-owned enterprises. “For all the years that I have followed politics and governance, I haven’t heard of such that the Chief Justice will be touring state-owned enterprises. I haven’t heard of that before,” he said. He argued that the Judiciary, as an independent arm of government, traditionally maintains a certain distance from the activities of the Executive and Legislature. “The Judiciary is supposed to be more or less independent. It’s an arm of government on its own; they don’t mingle with whether it’s the Legislature or the Executive,” he stated. Read also: Chief Justice praises MIIF, other SOEs, questions what Ghana was doing in past 8 years Mr Nkrumah said it was an established practice for members of the Judiciary to avoid public engagements that could potentially draw them into political or governance matters. “It is a well-known, established practice that the Judiciary doesn’t mingle, so you don’t see judges going around mingling in public,” he added. The Ofoase-Ayirebi MP said he was therefore uncertain about the circumstances that warranted the Chief Justice’s tours of the state institutions. He further noted that the Chief Justice had recently faced criticism over what some people perceived as his closeness to officials of the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC). Mr Nkrumah argued that the official visits and subsequent comments on the performance of state institutions could deepen concerns about the Judiciary becoming involved in matters traditionally associated with the Executive. “So, if upon that now there are official tours that are going on, it’s bewildering, and then I find it strange to hear some of these comments being made by the Judiciary,” he said. He stressed that the Judiciary must remain independent and avoid being drawn into political and governance debates. “My first reaction is that this is bewildering; it’s absolutely shocking. This is unprecedented. I haven’t seen that before, that the Judiciary will get involved at this level,” he added.

items.description: Entre gritos de “¡Pedro Sánchez, a prisión!” e “¡Invasores, expulsión!“, varios miles de personas ―50.000, según la Delegación de Gobierno― se concentraron este miércoles a última hora de la tarde frente al Ayuntamiento de Madrid convocadas formalmente para dar su respaldo a Ceuta tras la crisis por la entrada masiva de inmigrantes a finales de julio. Pronto se vio en la protesta de la capital que no se trataba solo de apoyar a los ceutíes, sino de manifestarse en contra del presidente del Gobierno, al que los concentrados dirigieron su ira por lo sucedido, coreando “¡Pedro Sánchez, hijo de puta!” y pidiendo que se le encarcele. Alberto Núñez Feijóo y Santiago Abascal, líderes del PP y Vox, que asistieron juntos pero sin coincidir a la protesta de Madrid, endurecieron su ofensiva contra el presidente del Gobierno, acusándolo de “mentir” a los españoles y de ser un “lacayo” de Marruecos y “un traidor” a España. items.title: Online fraud accounts for 47% of Ghana’s cyber incidents – CSA
items.description: Nearly half of cybersecurity incidents reported in Ghana between January and July 2026 involved online fraud, the Cyber Security Authority (CSA) has disclosed. The Director‑General of the CSA, Mr Divine Selase Agbeti, said the national Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT‑GH) recorded 3,876 incidents during the period, of which 1,818 cases, representing about 47 per cent, were linked to online fraud. He made the disclosure at the launch of the 2026 National Cyber Security Awareness Month (NCSAM) in Accra on the theme: “Securing Ghana’s Digital Finance Ecosystem: Building Trust Through Collaboration and Cyber Resilience.” Mr Agbeti said the figures demonstrated the increasing vulnerability of citizens, businesses and institutions to cyber‑enabled crime as digital financial services become more widely adopted. “Behind each figure is a citizen, family, merchant or institution that may have suffered financial loss, disruption, emotional distress or reputational damage,” he said. Mr Agbeti noted that while digital finance continued to drive inclusion and growth, the rapid adoption of mobile money, online banking, digital payments and e‑commerce platforms was creating new opportunities for criminals to exploit unsuspecting users. He said that global and local data suggested digital adoption was accelerating faster than cybersecurity awareness and protective measures, citing findings that many mobile phone users still did not employ basic security measures such as password protection. Mr Agbeti said the Bank of Ghana’s 2025 Fraud Report reinforced concerns, revealing that reported fraud cases across banks, specialised deposit‑taking institutions and payment service providers increased by 48 per cent, from 16,733 cases in 2024 to 24,778 cases in 2025, with a total value at risk of GH¢101 million. He said fraud within the payment service provider sector presented the most significant challenge, with electronic fraud incidents rising by 54 per cent and the value at risk increasing by 95 per cent, from GH¢19 million to GH¢37 million. Describing cybercrime as a direct threat to public confidence in the financial system, Mr Agbeti stressed that trust remained the cornerstone of digital finance. “Once customers believe that a mobile money wallet can be emptied without recourse, that an online merchant may be fraudulent, that a bank transfer can be diverted, or that personal data can be abused without consequence, confidence erodes,” he stated. Mr Agbeti warned financial institutions, fintech firms, payment service providers, insurers and merchants against treating cybersecurity merely as a regulatory obligation or an IT issue. “Cybersecurity cannot remain a compliance exercise done solely for the regulator or a technology project delegated solely to the IT department. It is a board‑level governance obligation and an operational resilience requirement,” he said. Mr Agbeti urged organisations to strengthen identity and access management systems, implement multi‑factor authentication, conduct regular vulnerability assessments, secure customer information and improve incident response capabilities. He cautioned that advances in artificial intelligence were making cybercrime more sophisticated through voice cloning, impersonation and social engineering attacks. Mr Agbeti called for stronger collaboration among regulators, financial institutions, telecommunications operators, law enforcement agencies and the public to combat cyber‑enabled fraud. He stressed the importance of timely incident reporting, intelligence sharing and coordinated responses, saying criminals often took advantage of delays and weak cooperation among institutions. Mr Agbetil lauded the role of the media in educating the public and preventing cyber scams, noting that informed reporting could help citizens identify fraudulent schemes and protect themselves. He urged Ghanaians to remain vigilant, verify suspicious requests, secure online accounts and promptly report incidents. “No institution should wait to become a victim before taking cybersecurity seriously. “Ghana’s digital finance future will be shaped not only by how quickly we innovate, but also by how safely we do so,” he said.

items.title: Rome declares security ‘red zone’ around the Colosseum to protect tourists amid violent crime incidents
items.description: Rome’s ancient Colosseum, where gladiators were once gored by wild animals to the delight of cheering crowds, has never exactly been associated with safety. Even in fiction, Henry James’ heroine “Daisy Miller” succumbed to malaria caught during a moonlight visit to the amphitheater. Today, the danger has a more modern twist. In July, a group of about 50 young people left police officers injured in an attack that involved shooting fireworks. Authorities say the incident was part of a pattern of increased crime around the historic area. In an effort to turn the tide on security issues at the Colosseum, Rome’s officials have now declared the area around the site a “red zone,” meaning that extra security has been deployed with greater powers to protect both residents and tourists, blaming the recent trouble on “predatory crimes and drug dealing” linked to urban decay. Imposed in late August, the zone will remain in place until December 24. Extra security has also been added near the city’s main Termini train station, St. Peter’s Basilica, and the Basilica of Santa Maria Maggiore, which has seen an increase in visitors since Pope Francis was laid to rest in a tomb there in April 2025. The new red zone will see local police presence enhanced around the clock alongside a military presence. Italy’s military already protects high-traffic tourist attractions with barriers and pop-up checkpoints. But armed officers dressed in camouflage alongside military vehicles have apparently not acted as enough of a deterrent to petty criminals. “Security is tight here, but I just saw a woman get pickpocketed,” Janelle Triton, an American tourist visiting the Colosseum site from Philadelphia, told CNN on Tuesday afternoon. She said the thief had gone by the time law enforcement was alerted. “We were told by our hotel not to come here at night though, so we have avoided the area.” The decline in safety at one of Rome’s most prestigious attractions comes despite millions of dollars spent on infrastructure improvements in recent years — investments which officials have admitted may actually be fueling crime. ‘Serious public emergency’ Lamberto Giannini, who’s responsible for security in Rome, says a new Colosseum metro station that was part of an $8.3 billion project to enhance the city’s underground subway system is one of the factors behind the rise in incidents. The station, which opened in December 2025, contains a multi-floor underground museum showcasing artifacts unearthed during years of construction work on a new metro line. But Giannini says it has also become a conduit for marginalized youth heading into Rome’s historical center to prey on both visitors and the residents who visit the area after the tourists have left. The red zone ordinance issued by Giannini states that existing security measures have proved inadequate in tackling a “serious public emergency” that presents a “risk of serious damage” to sensitive areas. It gives security officers greater powers to arrest suspected troublemakers or to order them to leave the area. A spokesperson for the prefect told CNN there would be no further comment on the issue, but a report in September is expected to detail what impact the red zone has had on crime.

items.title: US Open: Medvedev, Pegula advance as rain disrupts schedule
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Daniil Medvedev and Jessica Pegula advanced to the third round of the US Open on Wednesday as rain continued to disrupt the tournament schedule. Reuters reports that Medvedev, the 2021 champion, defeated American wildcard Sebastian Gorzny 6-1, 6-3, 7-5 on Louis Armstrong Stadium. The Russian was briefly frustrated when two birds landed on the net, forcing the chair umpire to order a point to be replayed. Medvedev regained his composure to complete the victory. Third seed Pegula needed just 56 minutes to beat compatriot and 2020 Australian Open champion Sofia Kenin 6-3, 6-1 on Arthur Ashe Stadium. Pegula will face 2021 Canadian Open runner-up Leylah Fernandez in the third round. Persistent rain on Tuesday had already disrupted the tournament, pushing some first-round matches on the outer courts into a fourth day. Elsewhere, American Alex Michelsen upset 16th seed Brandon Nakashima 6-3, 6-4, 6-4 to reach the third round. Sixth seed Alex de Minaur was scheduled to begin his campaign against Italian qualifier Andrea Guerrieri after his Tuesday match was postponed. Defending champion Carlos Alcaraz was also scheduled to face Portugal’s Jaime Faria, while three-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka was set to meet qualifier Polina Iatcenko. items.title: Incendies en Algérie : un « énorme » convoi de solidarité de la diaspora quitte Marseille
items.description: L’Algérie a été endeuillée par des incendies qui ont touché plusieurs wilayas du pays fin août. Après le choc, les Algériens font preuve d’une mobilisation extraordinaire pour soutenir les sinistrés. Les membres de la diaspora n’ont pas manqué de participer à cet élan populaire. Quelques heures seulement après les premières vidéos qui montrent l’ampleur des dégâts, une cagnotte a été lancée pour la diaspora afin qu'ils puissent venir en aide aux victimes des incendies . Elle a dépassé les 100.000 € en seulement 24 heures. Ce n’était là que le début, car l’élan de solidarité s'est renforcé et les initiatives se sont multipliées. Les convois destinés aux sinistrés débordent, au point que les responsables de la collecte appellent les donateurs à faire une pause. Le Djazair 2 se transforme en bateau humanitaire L’ampleur de la générosité est notamment constatée à Marseille, d’où un impressionnant convoi lancé par les membres de la diaspora aux victimes des incendies en Algérie. Dans une vidéo, diffusée hier 1ᵉʳ septembre par Al Jazeera, on peut voir ce convoi quitter le port de Marseille à bord d’un navire à destination de l’Algérie. On y voit plusieurs voitures chargées de produits de tout genre, embarquer dans le Djazair 2, le navire d’Algérie Ferries, qui s’est transformé en un véritable navire humanitaire. Il s’agit « d’une énorme caravane d’aides qui va de Marseille vers Jijel », titre le média qatari. Les véhicules, drapés de l’emblème national, appartiennent à des Algériens de l’étranger, qui n'ont pas hésité à traverser la Méditerranée pour venir en aide à leurs concitoyens. Voir cette publication sur Instagram Une publication partagée par الجزيرة (@aljazeera) Il s’agit d’une initiative individuelle de la part de plusieurs Algériens de France, voire d’autres pays européens, qui partent au secours des victimes des incendies en Algérie. Cette démarche de la diaspora ne fait que confirmer son attachement à son pays d’origine, participant ainsi à l’élan populaire qui se constate depuis plusieurs jours, avec d’innombrables convois qui se dirigent vers Jijel au départ des autres wilayas du territoire national. L’article Incendies en Algérie : un « énorme » convoi de solidarité de la diaspora quitte Marseille est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Migration à Sebta : la LMDDH fait état d’abus et réclame des enquêtes
items.description: Dans un rapport inquiétant qui soulève plusieurs questions liées au respect des droits de l'Homme et des droits des migrants, la Ligue marocaine de défense des droits de l’Homme (LMDDH) a indiqué avoir reçu des informations faisant état de plusieurs cas d'abus, notamment dans l'usage de la force, dans le cadre des événements migratoires de Sebta occupée. Le rapport présenté ce mercredi par l'ONG en conférence de presse et qui concerne les événements migratoires qui se sont déroulés le 30 et 31 juillet dernier, a détaillé plusieurs faits liés aux violations présumées des droits humains et aux conditions de prise en charge des migrants lors des tentatives de franchissement de Sebta et Melilla. Le document a également reconnu les violences et dégradations attribuées à certains migrants. La Ligue marocaine de défense des droits de l’Homme, citant des sources de terrain et sanitaires, a relevé des « bruits de tirs à balles réelles » lors des opérations de franchissement collectif vers les enclaves de Sebta et Melilla. Pour l'ONG, ces informations doivent elles aussi faire l’objet d’une vérification et d’une enquête officielle indépendante afin de déterminer s’il y a eu des décès liés à l’usage d’armes réglementaires et déterminer les responsabilités. L'organisation a ainsi appelé à « révéler l’identité de chaque victime, le lieu et l’heure du décès, sa cause médicale, les résultats de l’autopsie, les circonstances qui l’ont précédé ainsi que l’issue de l’enquête judiciaire ». En rejetant la « réduction des morts à une guerre des chiffres », l'ONG a insisté que « le droit à la vie ne signifie pas seulement s’abstenir de tuer arbitrairement une personne, mais impose aux États une obligation positive d’anticiper les risques et de les prévenir, d’organiser les opérations de sauvetage, d’évacuation et de secours, et d’intervenir immédiatement lorsque la noyade, les bousculades ou les chutes sont prévisibles ». Sur les chiffres, elle a souligné la « grande contradiction » entre les données présentées, en estimant qu’il ne s’agissait pas d’une « simple divergence comptable pouvant être tranchée en choisissant le chiffre le plus élevé ou le plus bas » , car « derrière chaque chiffre se trouve un être humain qui a un nom, un visage, une famille et un droit non négociable à connaître son sort ». La LMDDH a également insisté sur la précision des conditions réelles et des causes des décès de ces migrants estimant qu'on « ne peut pas se contenter d’annoncer que la plupart des victimes sont mortes noyées sans déterminer les circonstances individuelles de chaque décès et sans établir si des actes, des ordres ou des abstentions auxquels les forces de l’ordre auraient contribué et qui auraient pu être évités ont joué un rôle ». Ainsi, la Ligue a appelé à « l’ouverture d’une enquête rapide, indépendante et efficace sur tout décès susceptible d’être lié à l’usage de la force, à des poursuites, à un retard dans les secours ou à un manquement dans la mise à disposition des moyens nécessaires ». Son président Adel Chikito, a estimé que la contradiction des chiffres témoigne d’un dysfonctionnement de la coordination entre les hôpitaux, la police, le parquet, les autorités frontalières et les institutions chargées de la conservation des dépouilles. « Le rapport fait également état d’allégations sérieuses concernant l’usage de la force par des services de sécurité marocains et espagnols, notamment des coups, des coups de pied, des jets de pierres ainsi que des traitements cruels ou dégradants », a-t-il dit, notant que l’organisation avait « documenté des images et des témoignages nécessitant un examen technique et judiciaire indépendant afin de déterminer le lieu et l’heure de chaque incident, l’identité des intervenants, la chaîne de commandement et la proportionnalité des moyens employés par rapport au danger existant » . Et d'ajouter : « Nous reconnaissons aux États le droit de protéger leurs frontières, d’empêcher les franchissements forcés et de protéger les populations, les biens et les forces de sécurité, mais la légitimité de l’objectif ne rend pas tous les moyens légitimes» . « La force ne doit être utilisée qu’en cas de nécessité, de manière proportionnée et après épuisement des moyens les moins dommageables, tout en garantissant les secours, la documentation des faits et la reddition de comptes », a-t-il encore affirmé. Par ailleurs, concernant les actes de violence et de dégradation attribués à certains participants aux tentatives de franchissement, le rapport a également noté des « jets de pierres, de dégradations de biens, de véhicules incendiés et de blessés parmi les forces publiques et les citoyens ». Sur ce point, l'ONG a souligné que sa position était claire et qu '« aucune protection des droits humains ne saurait soustraire l’auteur d’un crime à sa responsabilité, et il ne peut être justifié de s’en prendre aux habitants, aux agents de sécurité ou aux biens ». Toutefois, le responsable a souligné que « la responsabilité pénale est individuelle et qu’un acte commis par une personne ou un groupe ne peut servir de prétexte pour punir collectivement des milliers de personnes ou les priver d’eau, de soins et de protection juridique ». Il a insisté sur le principe suivant : « criminaliser l’acte, et non le groupe ; engager des responsabilités individuelles, et non exercer une vengeance collective ». Le rapport s’est également intéressé à la situation des femmes et des filles, relevant que « les conditions de sommeil en plein air, l’absence de sanitaires séparés et sûrs, ainsi que l’insuffisance de la protection, de l’éclairage et de la surveillance les ont exposées au harcèlement et aux violences sexuelles ». « Des témoignages de femmes faisant état de harcèlements et de tentatives d’agression répétées ont été recueillis, notamment pendant la nuit ou lorsqu’elles se rendaient aux toilettes », a-t-il fait observer. Le rapport fait, de même, état de données médicales et judiciaires concernant des tentatives de viol et des agressions sexuelles visant des mineures, notant que ces faits démontrent que « les violences sexuelles ne constituent pas une conséquence marginale de la crise, mais un risque prévisible auquel il aurait fallu se préparer en mettant en place des espaces sûrs pour les femmes et les filles, des mécanismes confidentiels de signalement, une prise en charge médicale, psychologique et juridique immédiate, ainsi qu’une protection des victimes et des témoins contre les représailles et la stigmatisation ». Enfin, concernant la situation des enfants et les mineurs, la Ligue a souligné qu’ « un grand nombre d’entre eux se sont retrouvés dans une zone extrêmement dangereuse, dans les rues ou dans des centres d’accueil surpeuplés, certains étant séparés de leur famille ». « Le rapport fait état de témoignages concernant la poursuite de mineurs, des violences et des insultes à leur encontre, ainsi que de failles dans leur protection, leur hébergement et la détermination de leur âge » , a conclu Adel Chikito. The post Migration à Sebta : la LMDDH fait état d’abus et réclame des enquêtes appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Interior Ministry investigated Gomoa-Effutu boundary concerns before clashes – A Plus
items.description: Gomoa Central Member of Parliament, Kwame Asare Obeng, popularly known as A Plus, has dismissed suggestions that the government failed to act on warnings about a potential violent confrontation over a land dispute between communities in the Gomoa and Effutu areas. According to him, the Ministry of the Interior and other state institutions took steps to investigate concerns he had raised before the recent violent clashes at New Winneba and surrounding communities. The clashes, believed to have been triggered by a land dispute involving residents of Effutu and Gomoa, left three people dead and 15 others injured. Speaking on Joy FM’s Top Story on Wednesday, September 2, A Plus said he began efforts to clarify the boundaries between Gomoa Central and Effutu shortly after becoming a Member of Parliament. “Government didn’t fail. The Interior Minister did everything he had to do,” he said. He explained that he first wrote to the Lands Commission requesting clarity on the boundaries between Gomoa Central and Effutu to prevent potential confrontations over administrative and traditional boundaries. According to him, the Commission subsequently provided him with a comprehensive report identifying the respective lands belonging to Gomoa and Effutu. A Plus said he also wrote to the Ministry of Local Government to seek clarification on the boundaries of the Gomoa Central District and received a response. “And they gave me a reply. When I received those correspondence, I wrote to the Ministry of Interior and stated that, based on the correspondence that I have received from the two institutions, this is Gomoa and this is Efutu.” He said there was a particular area located deep within Gomoa where votes cast during elections were counted as part of the Effutu constituency. “There’s a particular area in my constituency where votes that are cast there are counted in a different constituency,” he said. A Plus explained that he sought to understand the Legislative Instrument that established the Gomoa Central District and the circumstances that led to the arrangement. He said the Ministry of the Interior subsequently conducted its own investigations and research into the matter. According to him, the Ministry later communicated its findings to the Ghana Police Service and called for the necessary corrections to be made. “The Ministry of Interior also did its own investigation. They did their own research and they wrote to the Ghana Police Service telling them that this is the situation and so they have to correct it,” he said.

items.title: Conakry : l’ex-procureur Algassimou Diallo entendu à huis clos ce mercredi à la Cour suprême
items.description: Entendu dans le cadre de la phase d'instruction de son dossier, l’ancien magistrat Algassimou Diallo a été reçu ce mercredi 2 août 2026 au siège de la Cour suprême, à Conakry. L'audition s'est déroulée sous une stricte surveillance sécuritaire et à huis clos, avec un accès rigoureusement interdit à la presse, nous a été confirmée sur place par une source proche du dossier. Si la nature exacte des chefs d'accusation n'a pas été révélée, l'ouverture officielle de la procédure marque une étape décisive. À la sortie, les conseils de l'ancien magistrat ont quitté les lieux sans faire de déclaration commune. Le dossier étant déjà en instruction chez le juge d’instruction. ​Après une longue journée d'audition, l'ancien procureur est sorti de la Cour suprême aux environs de 19h10 sous haute escorte de la police. Vêtu d'une chemise en bazin LEPI et d'un pantalon noir, il marchait avec nonchalance. Il a ensuite été reconduit vers la prison civile de Coyah, où il est détenu. ​Pour rappel, le 18 août dernier, le ministre de la Justice, Garde des Sceaux, prenait une mesure conservatoire ordonnant la suspension d'Algassimou Diallo de son poste d'avocat général près la Cour suprême. Le 20 août 2026, le Conseil supérieur de la magistrature (CSM), réuni en instance disciplinaire, prononçait sa révocation définitive, une sanction entérinée dès le lendemain par un décret présidentiel officialisant sa radiation des effectifs de la magistrature. ​Figure judiciaire bien connue du grand public, l'ancien procureur de la République près le tribunal de première instance de Dixinn s'était notamment illustré lors du procès historique du massacre du 28 septembre 2009.

items.title: Tunis | Grandes surfaces : Injection quotidienne de 2,3 millions de bouteilles d’eau minérale
items.description: Afin de répondre à une pression sans précédent sur le marché, près de 2,3 millions de bouteilles d'eau minérale sont désormais distribuées chaque jour dans les grandes surfaces du Grand Tunis. C'est du moins, ce qu'annonce Hedi Baccour, président de la Chambre syndicale des grandes surfaces commerciales, dans une déclaration accordée à Mosaïque FM, ce mercredi 2 septembre 2026. Cette mesure exceptionnelle vise à désamorcer les tensions d'approvisionnement, alors que les hypermarchés représentent habituellement uniquement 5 % de la consommation nationale d'eau embouteillée. Cette forte demande s'inscrit dans un contexte particulièrement tendu rappelle Hedi Baccour, qui a en effet révélé que le stock régulateur national, qui compte habituellement entre 40 et 50 millions de bouteilles, a été entièrement épuisé avant la mi-juillet 2026. Face à cette situation critique, les producteurs prévoient de revoir à la hausse le volume de ce stock stratégique pour prévenir d'éventuelles pénuries lors des prochaines années. Pour rappel, la régulation des circuits de distribution sur l'ensemble du territoire national a d'ailleurs été au cœur d'une récente réunion de travail entre les professionnels du secteur et le ministère du Commerce, afin d'assurer un approvisionnement équilibré dans toutes les régions du pays. items.title: Chief Justice praises MIIF, other SOEs, questions what Ghana was doing in past 8 years
items.description: Chief Justice Paul Baffoe-Bonnie has praised the performance of the Minerals Income Investment Fund (MIIF) and other public institutions under the current administration, saying some of the developments he has witnessed have left him wondering what Ghana was doing over the past eight years. Speaking during a visit to MIIF on Wednesday, September 2, the Chief Justice said he had been impressed by what he had seen at the institution and what he had heard about the performance of other state entities. He said a visit to the Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT) earlier in the day had further reinforced his impression that some public institutions were now performing significantly better. “I must congratulate you. I mean, you have done marvellously well. See, because sometimes when we hear the things that you have done, the things that some organisations are doing now, we wonder; some of us keep wondering what really we have been doing in the past eight years,” he said. The Chief Justice said the information he received during his visit to SSNIT was particularly striking, especially against the backdrop of previous plans involving some of the institution’s assets. “We’ve just come back from SSNIT, we went to SSNIT this morning, and the kind of things that we heard, and we hear, we even heard before we went there, what we were told, if you compare that to the fact that not too long ago, SSNIT was preparing to sell its prized assets like Labadi Beach Hotel, you wonder how Ghana could have sunk so low,” he added. His comments amount to a strong endorsement of the performance of public institutions under the current government and an implicit comparison between the present administration and the previous eight-year period under the New Patriotic Party (NPP). The remarks have generated debate because of the constitutional position occupied by the Chief Justice and the Judiciary’s obligation to maintain independence from the executive and political parties. A judiciary under scrutiny The timing and context of the comments are particularly significant given the controversy that surrounded Justice Baffoe-Bonnie’s elevation to the country’s highest judicial office. He became Acting Chief Justice in April 2025 after President John Dramani Mahama suspended then-Chief Justice Gertrude Torkornoo following the determination of a prima facie case against her and the commencement of an Article 146 process. Justice Baffoe-Bonnie was the most senior Justice of the Supreme Court at the time and therefore assumed the acting position. President Mahama subsequently nominated him as substantive Chief Justice in September 2025 following Mrs Torkornoo’s removal from office. Parliament approved his nomination in November by 163 votes to 69, after a contentious process in which the NPP Minority raised objections and ultimately boycotted his vetting. The Minority argued that the appointment process should not proceed while legal challenges to Mrs Torkornoo’s removal were still pending. It also raised concerns about Justice Baffoe-Bonnie’s involvement in Supreme Court proceedings connected to the removal process and what it described as a potential conflict of interest. Justice Baffoe-Bonnie, however, rejected suggestions that his elevation was politically motivated. During his vetting, he defended his record and said his career progression was based on merit and long service. He also pledged to provide bipartisan leadership and uphold judicial independence.

items.title: El informe de la Policía apunta que agentes marroquíes “guiaron” la entrada de migrantes a Ceuta
items.description: El informe que el Centro Nacional de Inmigración y Fronteras (CENIF) de la Policía ha entregado en la Audiencia Nacional analiza imágenes y mensajes de redes sociales y habla de “permisividad” de las Fuerzas de seguridad marroquíes. En el documento, al que ha tenido acceso EL PAÍS, la Policía concluye que agentes de Rabat participaron en la entrada masiva de migrantes a Ceuta los días 30 y 31 de julio “guiando el cruce a través del agua”, en base al análisis que han realizado de entrevistas de migrantes en medios de comunicación y de imágenes en redes sociales. La Policía incluye una recopilación fotográfica de supuestos agentes marroquíes uniformados e incide en que no se trató de “algo accidental”, sino que “en comparación con otros procesos de entrada previos” en 2021 y 2024, en esta ocasión la “finalidad migratoria” operó solo como una “cobertura formal” para “dirigir un flujo masivo de personas a Ceuta”. items.title: Trump suggère de rebaptiser le détroit d'Ormuz à son nom
items.description: Le président américain, Donald Trump a proposé mercredi de renommer le détroit d'Ormuz en «détroit Trump» quelques jours après avoir signé un décret pour changer le nom du «lac Ontario», situé à la frontière canadienne, en «lac Amérique». «Maintenant que nous en avons le contrôle, devrions-nous rebaptiser le détroit d'Ormuz détroit Trump?», a écrit le président américain sur sa plateforme Truth Social. Ce passage maritime stratégique est en fait verrouillé par Téhéran depuis le début de la guerre, déclenchée le 28 février par des frappes israélo-américaines sur l'Iran. Les États-Unis mènent en réaction un blocus des ports iraniens. Mi-août, le président américain avait publié une carte montrant le détroit d'Ormuz et le décrivant comme un «nouveau territoire américain», reprenant une idée qu'il avait exprimée quelques jours auparavant sur un ton qui laissait penser à une plaisanterie. Ce n'était pas la première fois que Donald Trump, confronté à un obstacle de politique étrangère, lançait ainsi une suggestion surprenante ou menaçante d'annexion d'un territoire étranger. Depuis son retour au pouvoir, il a menacé de faire du Canada le «51ᵉ» État américain, de s’emparer du Groenland et même évoqué une prise de contrôle de la bande de Gaza, sans passer à l'acte. Il a aussi rebaptisé en janvier 2025 le golfe du Mexique en «Golfe de l'Amérique» , une décision contestée par Mexico. Sa dernière remarque concernant le détroit d'Ormuz intervient alors qu'une issue pacifique au conflit entre l'Iran et les États-Unis semble lointaine. Mi-juin, les deux belligérants avaient signé un protocole d'accord censé déboucher sur un règlement durable, qui n'a rien donné. Après un mois de calme, les hostilités viennent de reprendre avec des frappes américaines près du détroit d'Ormuz et des réponses iraniennes contre des intérêts américains au Moyen-Orient. Washington et Téhéran posent des conditions a priori irréconciliables à la réouverture du détroit, passage névralgique pour le commerce mondial de pétrole. items.title: FDA recalls Arcan Bitters over undeclared erectile dysfunction drug
items.description: The Food and Drugs Authority (FDA) has ordered the recall of Arcan Bitters from the Ghanaian market after laboratory tests found the alcoholic drink had been adulterated with Sildenafil Citrate, a prescription-only drug used to treat erectile dysfunction. The FDA has given the manufacturer, Unni Associates Company Limited, 14 days to withdraw the product from the market. The company’s manufacturing facility at Parkoso in the Asokore Mampong Municipality of the Ashanti Region has also been shut down. In a public notice issued on Wednesday, September 2, the FDA said laboratory analysis of Arcan Bitters, labelled as containing 35% alcohol by volume, established the presence of Sildenafil Citrate. Sildenafil Citrate is a Phosphodiesterase Type 5 (PDE5) inhibitor and is not permitted in food products. The FDA said Arcan Bitters is registered with the Authority as an alcoholic beverage and must therefore not contain any drug substance.

items.title: Burkina : le ministre de la Sécurité lance « Yiri Dèmè » pour améliorer la survie des arbres plantés le long du contournement
items.description: Burkina : le ministre de la Sécurité lance « Yiri Dèmè » pour améliorer la survie des arbres plantés le long du contournement Ouagadougou, 2 sept. 2026 (AIB)-Le ministre de la Sécurité, Mahamadou Sana, a lancé mercredi les activités de la brigade « Yiri Dèmè », mise en place pour améliorer le taux de survie des arbres plantés le long de la voie de contournement de Ouagadougou, à travers leur entretien, leur arrosage, leur suivi et le régarnissage des plants. La brigade « Yiri Dèmè », qui signifie en langue dioula « aider l’arbre, entretenir l’arbre », a également pour mission de poursuivre les opérations de reboisement dans les zones non encore couvertes et de sensibiliser les populations riveraines et les usagers à la préservation des plantations. Pour le ministre de la Sécurité, Mahamadou Sana, la mise en place de cette brigade répond à la nécessité d’assurer la survie des arbres plantés depuis 2024 le long de la voie de contournement, avec pour objectif de le porter à un taux de survie de 100 % contre 75 % actuellement. Le ministre de la Sécurité, Mahamadou Sana, a indiqué que le taux de survie des arbres plantés à l’occasion des Journées nationales de l’arbre est passé d’environ 28 % en 2018 à 49 % en 2025, assurant que la mise en place de la brigade devrait permettre d’améliorer davantage ce taux. Le ministre de la Sécurité a annoncé que l’initiative devrait progressivement s’étendre aux autres régions afin de contribuer au reverdissement des routes nationales. Il a également appelé les populations riveraines à accompagner la brigade dans la protection des arbres, notamment en luttant contre la divagation des animaux et les feux de brousse. Le directeur général des Eaux et Forêts, le colonel Bernabé Kaboré, a indiqué que la « Yiri Dèmè » a pour mission d’assurer un arrosage permanent et un entretien régulier des plants, suivant un calendrier adapté aux saisons et aux besoins spécifiques de chaque espèce. Elle devra également surveiller les plantations et sensibiliser les populations riveraines ainsi que les usagers de la voie de contournement sur la nécessité de préserver les arbres et poursuivre les opérations de reboisement afin de compléter les zones qui ne sont pas encore couvertes par les plantations. Une autre mission essentielle consiste à assurer une veille sécuritaire permanente sur l’ensemble de sa zone d’intervention, en complémentarité avec les autres forces de sécurité intérieure et les initiatives locales de sécurité. Pour mener ces missions, des ressources humaines et des moyens matériels ont été mobilisés. Trois forages ont notamment été réalisés à ce jour afin de faciliter la disponibilité de l’eau pour l’arrosage. Des tricycles-citernes, un véhicule, des motos ainsi que divers équipements de reboisement et d’entretien ont également été prévus. La brigade dispose déjà de six postes au niveau des différentes intersections avec les routes nationales. Le taux de réalisation des plantations le long de la voie de contournement est estimé à environ 75 %, sur un objectif de 480 000 plants. Six espèces locales ont été sélectionnées pour cette phase, notamment Kaya senegalensis, Adansonia digitata, Vitex doniana, Pterocarpus erinaceus, Afzelia africana et Ceiba pentandra, selon le colonel Kaboré. Agence d’information du Burkina YOS/ata

items.title: 18-yr-old arrested over alleged plot to kidnap Kylian Mbappe
items.description: Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappe was among 26 wealthy individuals allegedly targeted in a kidnapping plot uncovered by French authorities. French newspaper Le Parisien reported that the alleged plot was orchestrated by an 18-year-old identified as Clement L, who was reportedly directing activities from prison using two mobile phones. The individuals targeted allegedly included footballers, rappers, wealthy businessmen, jewelers and other high-profile figures. According to the report, authorities discovered the names and addresses of the 26 targets on phones seized by prison guards. Mbappe was reportedly among those identified on the list. Clement L had previously been placed in pre-trial detention over allegations relating to pimping and organised robbery. He had also been jailed for armed robbery after being identified as one of two men involved in an attack on a watchmaker in Paris. Despite being held in custody, he allegedly continued issuing instructions through Snapchat under the alias “Lester Z”. A source close to the investigation told Le Parisien that the contents of the two phones seized from the teenager were “highly revealing”. “He also wanted to go after a rapper and the footballer Kylian Mbappe,” the source said. The teenager reportedly denied being the mastermind behind the plot when questioned by authorities and asked to be released from solitary confinement. He told investigators that he had dropped out of school while studying for a vocational qualification in cooking but wanted to resume his studies and become a chef. His request was rejected, with authorities ruling that he should remain in solitary confinement as investigations into the alleged kidnapping plot continue. items.title: Cambodia Court Sentences 3 Activists to 7 Years in Prison
items.description: Click to expand Image The Phnom Penh Municipal Court, Cambodia, January 14, 2020. © 2020 Heng Sinith/AP Photo The government-controlled municipal court in Phnom Penh on September 2, 2026 sentenced three activists to seven years in prison for allegedly plotting against the government. They were 25-year-old student leader Thy Thorn and two political opposition activists, Soeung Kunthea and Mean Chanthon. Kunthea and Chanthon were arrested in Thailand in November 2024 and summarily deported to Cambodia to face trial, despite being recognized as refugees by the United Nations refugee agency. The long sentences on baseless charges are the latest abuse of the judicial system by the ruling Cambodian People’s Party in its efforts to silence critical voices in the country. Thorn, Chanthon and Kunthea were among at least 94 people arrested by Cambodian authorities in 2024 amid a wave of criticisms of the Cambodia–Laos–Vietnam Development Triangle Area (CLV), a controversial economic development plan among the three governments established in 2004. The Cambodian government later withdrew from the agreement after the public outcry. Thorn was apparently arrested because of his position as a vice-president of the Khmer Student Intelligent League Association, a student group that is active in raising social and environmental issues. The government has repeatedly targeted the student association’s leadership in the past over their activism. The group’s president, Koet Saray, is currently serving a four-year prison sentence on incitement charges. In February, the UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention determined that Saray’s detention was arbitrary and in violation of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, which Cambodia ratified in 1992. The Cambodian People’s Party pressured many of those arrested for criticizing the CLV development plan to confess and join the ruling party in exchange for their release. These confessions were then used to discredit critics and activists as part of the Cambodian government’s systematic campaign to undermine the political standing of opposition groups. Those unwilling to confess are now being punished with lengthy prison sentences. Cambodian authorities should immediately release Thorn, Kunthea and Chanthon, and quash their convictions. Governments, especially those attending the Francophonie Summit in Phnom Penh in November, should use their influence to pressure the Cambodian government to release all political prisoners and end its repression of peaceful critics.
